title: The three little pigs.
lines: Once upon a time there were three little pigs.
They lived with their mummy in a little house on the farm.
One day Mummy Pig said: You're big now.
It's time for each of you to build your own house.
But watch out for the big bad wolf!
The first little pig was a bit lazy.
I'll build my house of straw, he said.
That's really quick, and then I can play for the rest of the day.
And sure enough, his straw house was ready in half an hour.
The second little pig wanted to be finished quickly too.
I'll build my house of sticks and wood, he said.
Knock, knock, knock.
After an hour his wooden house was ready.
The third little pig was very sensible.
I'll build my house of bricks, she said.
It takes a long time, but it's strong.
She laid brick on brick, brick on brick, all day long.
Her brothers laughed at her.
Come and play!
No, said the third little pig, I'll work first.
In the evening the big bad wolf came.
He knocked on the door of the straw house.
Little pig, little pig, let me come in!
No, no, not by the hair on my chinny-chin-chin!
Then I'll huff and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house down!
And the wolf blew: Whoooosh!
The straw house flew away.
The first little pig ran as fast as he could to the wooden house.
The wolf came after him.
Little pigs, little pigs, let me come in!
No, no, not by the hair on our chinny-chin-chins!
Then I'll huff and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house down!
Whooooosh!
Crack!
The wooden house fell down.
The two little pigs ran to their sister's brick house.
Quick, come in!
she shouted, and she locked the door.
Click.
The wolf arrived.
Little pigs, little pigs, let me come in!
No, no, not by the hair on our chinny-chin-chins!
The wolf huffed and puffed.
Whoooooooosh!
He blew until he went completely red.
But the brick house stayed standing.
Not a single brick moved.
Then the wolf tried to climb in through the chimney.
But the clever little pig had put a big pot of water on the fire.
The wolf felt the hot steam on his tail.
Ow, ow, ow!
he shouted, and he jumped out of the chimney and ran away, into the forest.
He never came back.
The three little pigs danced for joy.
And the next day the two brothers helped their sister.
Together they built two more brick houses, next to each other.
Because working hard, they said, is worth it.
